messages.subject: Skew normals likelihood bug?
parts:
Hi guys,
I'm trying out some skew-normal distributions, the mean of the likelihood seems to skewing towards the opposite direction of the priors: 

library(rstan)
stanmodelcode <- "
data {
  real y;
} 
parameters {
  real p;
  real p2;
} 
model {
  p ~ skew_normal(1, 10,-1000);
  y ~ skew_normal(p2, 10,-1000);
} 
"
dat <- list(y = 1); 
fit <- stan(model_code = stanmodelcode, 
            data = dat, iter = 66666, chains = 2,
            verbose = TRUE) 
library(ggmcmc)
s <- ggs(fit)
ggs_histogram(s)


I wasn't expecting that to happen, should I? If so why?, or is this a bug? 


best regards,
Jökull Snæbjarnarson

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Skew normals likelihood bug?
parts:
It looks approximately correct. For this model:

parameters {
real theta;
}
model {
theta ~ skew_normal(1, 10, -1000);
}

I get

======================================
> fit <- stan("skew.stan", control=list(stepsize=0.001, adapt_delta=0.9999), fit=fit)

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'skew' NOW (CHAIN 1).
...
Chain 4, Iteration: 2000 / 2000 [100%] (Sampling)
# Elapsed Time: 0.506487 seconds (Warm-up)
# 0.113476 seconds (Sampling)
# 0.619963 seconds (Total)

Warning messages:
1: There were 1409 divergent transitions after warmup. Increasing adapt_delta may help.
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

> print(fit)
Inference for Stan model: skew.
4 chains, each with iter=2000; warmup=1000; thin=1;
post-warmup draws per chain=1000, total post-warmup draws=4000.

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
theta -6.73 0.34 5.88 -20.67 -10.19 -5.52 -2.13 0.78 308 1.01
lp__ 0.22 0.04 0.67 -1.65 0.07 0.48 0.64 0.69 363 1.01

Samples were drawn using NUTS(diag_e) at Mon Jan 4 12:21:00 2016.
For each parameter, n_eff is a crude measure of effective sample size,
and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor on split chains (at
convergence, Rhat=1).
==================================


The actual mean is -7.0, so we're within the MCMC std error, but I'm worried
because of the divergent translations and low n_eff. Going up to 20K iterations,
I get this:

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
theta -6.93 0.10 5.97 -21.28 -10.35 -5.74 -2.22 0.70 3517 1
lp__ 0.20 0.01 0.70 -1.79 0.05 0.46 0.64 0.69 3746 1

So I think what's happening is that it's finding it hard to get out into
the negative tail of this distribution.

But you probably want to reparameterize to get rid of the divergent
transitions (these are cases where there is an arithmetic underflow or
overflow in the basic math). We're probably not doing a good job on
the log(1 + erf) term, which should really have some tricks played on
it algebraically.

In fact, looking at the implementation that's in there now, it's
pretty bad in terms of efficiency (lots of repeated subterms), but
it should be about as good as we can do for arithmetic stability
until we write a composed log-erfc (the code uses the erf/erfc identities
correctly).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Skew normals likelihood bug?
parts:
It works just fine for me. I use this program to generate data:


skew.stan
-------------------------

parameters {
real theta;
}
model {
theta ~ skew_normal(1, 10, -1000);
}

and this program to fit it:


skew-fit.stan
-----------------------------------
data {
int<lower=0> N;
vector[N] y;
}
parameters {
real mu;
}
model {
y ~ skew_normal(mu, 10, -1000);
}

and it recovers the parameter very precisely:

Inference for Stan model: skew-fit.

4 chains, each with iter=2000; warmup=1000; thin=1;
post-warmup draws per chain=1000, total post-warmup draws=4000.
mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat

For each parameter, n_eff is a crude measure of effective sample size,
and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor on split chains (at
convergence, Rhat=1).

=========================

In R:

> library(rstan);

> fit <- stan("skew.stan", control=list(adapt_delta=0.99, stepsize=0.01));

> y <- extract(fit)$theta;

> fit2 <- stan("skew-fit.stan", data=list(N=length(y), y = y));

> print(fit2);


- Bob
